{
  "verdict": "fix",
  "issues": [
    "The summary states the API has a seven-field task model, but the Task schema defines six fields (id, title, description, completed, createdAt, updatedAt). The field count is inconsistent.",
    "The API is described as using RFC 9457-style errors, but the Error schema does not follow RFC 9457's problem details format (it lacks the type, title, status, detail, and instance members). It is a custom error format, not RFC 9457-compliant.",
    "The Task response schema does not mark id, createdAt, and updatedAt as readOnly. This can mislead clients into thinking these fields are writable, even though request schemas intentionally omit them.",
    "The GET /tasks operation has no error responses defined, leaving failure behavior unspecified for clients."
  ],
  "suggestions": [
    "Update the summary to say 'six-field task model' or add the intended seventh field (e.g., a dueDate or priority field) to the schema.",
    "Either align the Error schema with RFC 9457 by adding required members like type (and recommended title/status/detail/instance), or explicitly label the format as a custom compact error object.",
    "Add readOnly: true to id, createdAt, and updatedAt in the Task schema for clarity.",
    "Add a default or 500 error response for GET /tasks to fully specify the API contract.",
    "Consider using application/merge-patch+json as the media type for PATCH /tasks/{taskId} to conform to merge patch semantics."
  ]
}
